rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descendants' proposed excuse is that their ancestors committed shirk and they were young offspring who followed them, so they should not be destroyed for their ancestors' deeds.
rows.anchor: أيها الذرية محتجين يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God reminded every descendant of the covenant to affirm tawhid, they cannot justify shirk by citing their parents.
rows.anchor: فلا يمكنهم الاحتجاج بكون الآباء على الشرك بعد تذكير الله بأخذ الميثاق بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains the signs so people may reflect on them and return from their present disbelief.
rows.anchor: ولكي يرجعوا عما هم عليه من الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person given proofs of tawhid who stripped himself of them was Balaam ibn Baura; he aided God's enemies against His allies by praying for them, and lost faith.
rows.anchor: أعان أعداء الله على أوليائه بدعائه، فنزع عنه الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many jinn and humans created for Hell are those upon whom wretchedness has become certain.
rows.anchor: وهم الذين حقت عليهم الشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts do not reason with them about good and guidance.
rows.anchor: لا يعقلون بها الخير والهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes fail to see the paths of guidance.
rows.anchor: ولهم أعين لا يبصرون بها } سبل الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ears fail to heed the admonitions of the Quran.
rows.anchor: ولهم آذان لا يسمعون بها } مواعظ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble livestock in eating and drinking while paying no heed to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: يأكلون ويشربون ولا يلتفتون إلى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are further astray than livestock because livestock obey God whereas the unbeliever does not.
rows.anchor: لأن الأنعام مطيعة لله، والكافر غير مطيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are heedless of the punishment awaiting in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: عما في الآخرة من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's beautiful names are the ninety-nine names.
rows.anchor: ولله الأسماء الحسنى } يعني: التسعة والتسعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should call upon God with these names, such as Allah, the Powerful, and the Knowing.
rows.anchor: فادعوه بها } كقولك: يا الله، يا قدير، يا عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deviate in God's names are polytheists who repurposed names for idols, adding or subtracting and deriving al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat from divine names.
rows.anchor: وهم المشركون عدلوا بأسماء الله عما هي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will receive recompense for their deeds in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: جزاء ما كانوا يعملون في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is for what people earned, and God is not unjust to His servants because His judgment concerns what He decrees.
rows.anchor: هذا العذاب { بما قدمت أيديكم } بما كسبتم وجنيتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers' pattern resembles Pharaoh's people: God punished them as He punished Pharaoh's people for disbelief.
rows.anchor: عادة هؤلاء في التكذيب كعادة آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is powerful, none can overcome Him, and He severely punishes those who disbelieve and deny His messengers.
rows.anchor: إن الله قوي } قادر لا يغلبه شيء { شديد العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fed Mecca's people after hunger, secured them from fear, and sent Muhammad to them; these were blessings He would not change had they not changed themselves.
rows.anchor: أطعم أهل مكة من جوع، وآمنهم من خوف، وبعث إليهم محمدا رسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their change was disbelief and ingratitude, so God removed their blessing and seized them; the verse then concerned the Jews of Qurayza.
rows.anchor: وتغييرهم كفرهم بها وتركهم شكرها، فلما غيروا ذلك غير الله ما بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is from the Arabs, descendants of Ishmael, so his people can understand him.
rows.anchor: من العرب من بني إسماعيل ليفهموا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people's hardship and every harm they suffer grieve him, and he is eager for them to believe; this addresses disbelievers who did not believe him.
rows.anchor: شديد عليه مشقتكم وكل مضرة تصيبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Toward believers, the messenger is compassionate and merciful.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر أنه { بالمؤمنين رؤوف رحيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those turning away are the polytheists and hypocrites; the Prophet is to say that God is sufficient for him.
rows.anchor: يعني: المشركين والمنافقين { فقل حسبي الله } أي: الذي يكفيني الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He trusts and relies upon God, Lord of the Throne, singled out because it is the greatest of God's creation.
rows.anchor: خص بالذكر لأنه أعظم ما خلق الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith guides believers to gardens as its reward.
rows.anchor: أي: إلى الجنان ثوابا لهم بإيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer in Paradise is to glorify God; whenever they desire something and say this, they receive it, then praise God after enjoying it.
rows.anchor: كلما اشتهوا شيئا قالوا: سبحانك اللهم، فجاءهم ما يشتهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is told not to grieve or be distressed.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تحزن ولا تغتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Building the ark before God's eyes means in His sight and under His protection, like one who sees and can ward off harm; God revealed how to build it because Noah did not know the craft.
rows.anchor: بمرأى منا، وتأويله: بحفظنا إياك حفظ من يراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah must not debate with God about delaying the punishment of the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: لا تراجعني ولا تحاورني { في الذين ظلموا } في إمهالهم وتأخير العذاب عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people mock Noah for building the ark, he says he will mock them by marveling at their heedlessness of the approaching punishment.
rows.anchor: أي: لما يرون من صنعه الفلك { فإنا نسخر منكم } ونعجب من غفلتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will soon learn who receives humiliating punishment and who has the worst outcome.
rows.anchor: فسوف تعلمون من أخسر عاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command means the destruction of Noah's people; water burst from the baker's oven as the sign for Noah to board the ship.
rows.anchor: بعذابهم وهلاكهم { وفار التنور } بالماء، يعني: تنور الخابز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was commanded to take two of every kind, male and female, aboard the ark.
rows.anchor: في الفلك { من كل زوجين } من كل شيء له زوج { اثنين } ذكرا وأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was to take his children and household except those decreed to drown for disbelief: his wife Waghila and son Canaan; he also took those who believed, numbering eighty.
rows.anchor: يعني: من كان في علم الله أنه يغرق بكفره، وهو امرأته واغلة، وابنه كنعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' signs were the Torah and the laws revealed in it, while the clear authority was the staff.
rows.anchor: يريد: التوراة وما أنزل الله فيها من الأحكام { وسلطان مبين } وحجة بينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's command did not guide anyone to good.
rows.anchor: وما أمر فرعون برشيد } بمرشد إلى خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh leads his people ahead of him to Hell; bringing them there is an evil arrival.
rows.anchor: يتقدمهم إلى النار، وهو قوله: { فأوردهم النار } أدخلهم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were followed by a curse in this world, meaning drowning, and a curse on Judgment Day, meaning Hell; it is curse upon curse.
rows.anchor: يعني: الغرق { ويوم القيامة } يعني: ولعنة يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the destroyed towns, some still have standing walls, while others were razed until their traces disappeared.
rows.anchor: قائم بقيت حيطانه، وحصيد مخسوف به قد محي أثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not wrong them by punishment and destruction; they wronged themselves through disbelief and disobedience.
rows.anchor: بالعذاب والإهلاك { ولكن ظلموا أنفسهم } بالكفر والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their idols did not benefit or protect them from God; worshipping them only increased their ruin, affliction, and loss.
rows.anchor: ما نفعتهم وما دفعت عنهم { آلهتهم التي يدعون } يعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what is hidden in the heavens and earth, and every affair returns to Him at resurrection, leaving no authority to anyone else.
rows.anchor: أي: علم ما غاب عن العباد فيهما { وإليه يرجع الأمر كله } في المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not heedless of people's deeds: He rewards the good-doer for good and the wrongdoer for wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي: إنه يجزي المحسن بإحسانه، والمسيء بإساءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what is hidden from all creation and what creation witnesses; He is great in rank and exalted above the polytheists' claims.
rows.anchor: ما غاب عن جميع خلقه { والشهادة } وما شهده الخلق { الكبير } العظيم القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God equally knows the openly speaking and inwardly concealing person, and the visible and hidden one; hidden means concealed and sārib means apparent and moving along.
rows.anchor: علم الله سبحانه فيهم جميعا سواء، والمستخفي معناه: المختفي، والسارب: الظاهر المار على وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardian angels alternate between night and day, coming down to earth and protecting a person before and behind by God's command.
rows.anchor: ملائكة حفظة تتعاقب في النزول إلى الأرض، بعضهم بالليل، وبعضهم بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the decree arrives, the angels leave the person to it.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاء القدر خلوا بينه وبينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not remove a people's blessing until they commit acts of disobedience.
rows.anchor: لا يسلب قوما نعمة حتى يعملوا بمعاصيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills harm for a people, none can repel it, and no protector besides Him can manage their affair or ward off punishment.
rows.anchor: فلا مرد له } فلا رد له { وما لهم من دونه من وال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for a sign came from Meccan polytheists.
rows.anchor: نزلت في مشركي مكة حين طالبوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misguides whom He wills despite sending signs, which they failed to use as evidence.
rows.anchor: { قل إن الله يضل من يشاء } عن دينه، كما أضلكم بعدما أنزل من الآيات، وحرمكم الاستدلال بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides to His religion whoever turns back to the truth.
rows.anchor: يرشد إلى دينه { من أناب } رجع إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe is an appositive explaining those who turn back to God.
rows.anchor: الذين آمنوا } بدل من قوله: { من أناب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers love and find comfort and ease when they hear the remembrance of God; the tranquil hearts are believers' hearts.
rows.anchor: إذا سمعوا ذكر الله سبحانه وتعالى أحبوه واستأنسوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tuba is a tree planted by God Himself.
rows.anchor: وهي شجرة غرسها الله سبحانه بيده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation of Tuba is joy and delight of the eyes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فرح لهم وقرة أعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God sent earlier prophets, He sent Muhammad to a generation following earlier peoples to recite the Quran.
rows.anchor: كما أرسلنا الأنبياء قبلك { أرسلناك في أمة } في قرن { قد خلت } قد مضت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans denied the Merciful and said they knew that name only as the man of Yamama; Muhammad must affirm He is his Lord and sole deity.
rows.anchor: وهم يكفرون بالرحمن } وذلك أنهم قالوا: ما نعرف الرحمن إلا صاحب اليمامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to say that the Merciful whom they deny is his Lord and that there is no deity but Him.
rows.anchor: الرحمن الذي أنكرتم معرفته هو إلهي وسيدي { لا إله إلا هو }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who prefer worldly life to the afterlife, obstruct God's path, and seek to make it crooked are far from truth.
rows.anchor: يؤثرون ويختارون { الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ويصدون عن سبيل الله } ويمنعون الناس عن دين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each messenger spoke the language of his people so they could understand; after clarification, God misguides those who choose falsehood.
rows.anchor: بلغة قومه ليفهموا عنه، وهو معنى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides those who follow the truth.
rows.anchor: ويهدي من يشاء } باتباع الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sent with proofs of his prophethood and ordered to bring his people from shirk's darkness into the light of faith.
rows.anchor: بالبراهين التي دلت على صحة نبوته { أن أخرج قومك من الظلمات إلى النور } من الشرك إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was to remind his people of God's Days, meaning His blessings, exhorting them through encouragement and warning, promise and threat.
rows.anchor: وعظهم { بأيام الله } بنعمه، أي: بالترغيب والترهيب، والوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reminders are signs for those steadfast in obedience and grateful for God's blessings.
rows.anchor: لدلالات { لكل صبار } على طاعة الله { شكور } لأنعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known appointed time is the first trumpet blast, when all creatures die.
rows.anchor: يعني: النفخة الأولى حين يموت الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis says that, because God led him astray, he will adorn falsehood for Adam's descendants until they fall into it.
rows.anchor: أي: بسبب إغوائك إياي { لأزينن لهم } لأولاد آدم الباطل حتى يقعوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception of God's sincere servants means the monotheistic believers who made their religion sincere and free of shirk.
rows.anchor: أي: الموحدين المؤمنين الذي أخلصوا دينهم عن الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the path of servitude that leads back to God, who will recompense each according to deeds.
rows.anchor: هذا طريق علي { مستقيم } مرجعه إلي، فأجازي كلا بأعمالهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guided and chosen servants are beyond Satan's power or argument to lead them into shirk and misguidance.
rows.anchor: يعني: الذين هداهم واجتباهم { ليس لك عليهم سلطان } قوة وحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is the appointed destination of Iblis and all who follow the misguided.
rows.anchor: يريد: إبليس ومن تبعه من الغاوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell has seven gates, understood as seven layers stacked above one another, with a designated portion of Iblis's followers for each gate.
rows.anchor: سبعة أطباق، طبق فوق طبق { لكل باب منهم } من أتباع إبليس { جزء مقسوم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing avoid indecencies and major sins and dwell in gardens with springs of water and wine.
rows.anchor: للفواحش والكبائر { في جنات وعيون } يعين: عيون الماء والخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discerning are those who carefully and persistently observe until they recognize the true mark of a thing.
rows.anchor: أي: المتفرسين المتثبتين في النظر حتى يعرفوا حقيقة سمة الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's town lies on a lasting, unmistakable road that Quraysh take toward Syria.
rows.anchor: يعني: مدينة قوم لوط { لبسبيل مقيم } على طريق قومك إلى الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town's destruction is a lesson for believers, who take heed from it.
rows.anchor: لعبرة للمصدقين. يعني: إن المؤمنين اعتبروا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Thicket were Shuaib's people, owners of groves and trees.
rows.anchor: قوم شعيب، وكانوا أصحاب غياض وأشجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were punished by heat for several days, then fire blazed around them and destroyed them.
rows.anchor: بالعذاب. أخذهم الحر أياما، ثم اضطرم عليهم المكان نارا فهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the Thicket and Lot's town stood on an obvious road.
rows.anchor: يعني: الأيكة ومدينة قوم لوط { لبإمام مبين } لبطريق واضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of al-Hijr were Thamud, al-Hijr being the name of their valley; denying Salih counted as denying all messengers.
rows.anchor: يعني: قوم ثمود، والحجر اسم واديهم { المرسلين } يعين: صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs given to Thamud were the miracles made manifest in the she-camel.
rows.anchor: يعني: ما أظهر لهم من الآيات في الناقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock provide warmth through clothing and buildings made from hair, wool, and fur, and provide offspring, milk, and riding.
rows.anchor: يعني: ما تستدفئون به من الأكسية والأبنية من أشعارها وأصوافها وأوبارها { ومنافع } من النسل والدر والركوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock are beautiful when brought back to their resting place in the evening and when sent out to pasture in the morning.
rows.anchor: زينة { حين تريحون } تردونها إلى مراحها بالعشايا { وحين تسرحون } تخرجونها إلى المرعى بالغداة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels carry people's belongings to places they could not reach without great exertion; shiqq means hardship.
rows.anchor: أمتعتكم { إلى بلد } لو تكلفتم بلوغه على غير الإبل لشق عليكم، والشق: المشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates things people do not know and leaves them unnamed; God knows best what they are.
rows.anchor: لم يسمه، فالله أعلم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path to God's pleasure is Islam; this path is linked to the path in 15:41.
rows.anchor: أي: الإسلام والطريق المستقيم يؤدي إلى رضا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some paths are crooked, such as Judaism and Christianity.
rows.anchor: ومن السبيل { جائر } عادل مائل كاليهودية والنصرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God willed, He would guide everyone so they would not differ in religion.
rows.anchor: أرشدكم { أجمعين } حتى لا تختلفوا في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjected to people what He created on earth in varied forms and appearances, including animals and trees.
rows.anchor: أي: وسخر لكم ما خلق في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the sea navigable and available for diving, food such as fish, and adornments such as pearls and jewels.
rows.anchor: ذلله للركوب والغوص { لتأكلوا منه لحما طريا } السمك والحيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships cut through the water with their bows, and people travel in them for trade and profit from God's bounty.
rows.anchor: شواق للماء تدفعه بجؤجئها بصدرها { ولتبتغوا من فضله } لتركبوه للتجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed stable mountains so the earth would not shake, and made rivers such as the Nile, Euphrates, and Tigris, plus roads to towns so people can find their destinations.
rows.anchor: جبالا ثابتة { أن تميد } لئلا تميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The landmarks are mountains that mark routes by day, while stars guide people to routes and the direction of prayer on land and sea.
rows.anchor: يعني الجبال، وهي علامات الطرق بالنهار { وبالنجم } يعني: جميع النجوم { هم يهتدون } إلى الطرق والقبلة في البر والبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāṣiban means perpetually: obedience to God is always obligatory, so one should fear the Creator of everything, who commanded people not to associate another deity.
rows.anchor: دائما، أي: طاعته واجبة أبدا. { أفغير الله } الذي خلق كل شيء، وأمر أن لا تتخذوا معه إلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every blessing, such as bodily health, ample provision, wealth, and children, comes from God; when sickness or need strikes, people cry out to Him for help.
rows.anchor: من صحة جسم، أو سعة رزق، أو إمتاع بمال وولد، فكل ذلك من الله، { ثم إذا مسكم الضر } الأسقام والحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the distress is removed, some disbelieve in God and associate others with Him.
rows.anchor: يعني: من كفر بالله، وأشرك بعد كشف الضر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny God's gift; the command to enjoy yourselves is a threat that they will learn the outcome.
rows.anchor: ليجحدوا نعمة الله فيما فعل بهم { فتمتعوا } أمر تهديد { فسوف تعلمون } عاقبة أمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭā Hā means O man.
rows.anchor: طه } يا رجل. { وما أنزلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran was not sent to make the Prophet toil from excessive effort; he prayed all night in Mecca until his feet swelled, and disbelievers said he suffered by leaving their religion, so this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: لتتعب بكثرة الجهد، وذلك أنه كان يصلي الليل كله بمكة حتى تورمت قدماه، وقال له الكفار: إنك لتشقى بترك ديننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is a reminder and admonition for whoever fears God.
rows.anchor: أي: ما أنزلناه إلا تذكرة، موعظة { لمن يخشى } يخاف الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿulā is the plural of al-ʿulyā.
rows.anchor: ممن خلق الأرض والسموات العلى } جمع العليا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss of istawā is that the Merciful attended to His creation, as in 2:29; the source also glosses it as istawlā, meaning prevailed.
rows.anchor:
استوى } [أي: أقبل على خلقه، كقوله:
ثم استوى إلى السماء
مع أنه أعظم المخلوقات]، أي: استولى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God perfected each created thing in a form useful to it and most suitable for its purpose, then guided it to its livelihood.
rows.anchor: أتقن كل شيء مما خلق، وخلقه على الهيئة التي بها ينتفع، والتي هي أصلح وأحكم لما يراد منه { ثم هدى } أي: هداه لمعيشته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses answered, Pharaoh asked about the deeds of earlier generations.
rows.anchor: ثم سأله فرعون عن أعمال الأمم الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh asks about the condition of past generations; Moses answers that their deeds are preserved with God and they will be recompensed.
rows.anchor: فأجابه موسى عليه السلام بأن أعمالهم محفوظة عند الله يجازون بها، وهو قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book containing their deeds is the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: علمها عند ربي في كتاب } وهو اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not err or leave an unbeliever without retribution, and does not forget a monotheist before rewarding that person.
rows.anchor: لا يخطىء، ومعناه: لا يترك من كفر به حتى ينتقم منه { ولا ينسى } من وحده حتى يجازيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the earth a bed and made its paths easy; the water from heaven means rain.
rows.anchor: فراشا { وسلك لكم فيها سبلا } وسهل لكم فيها طرقا { وأنزل من السماء ماء } يريد: المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' answer ends with the rain; the discourse then shifts to God's first-person plural, bringing forth varied kinds of plants with different colors and tastes.
rows.anchor: وتم ها هنا جواب موسى، ثم تلون الخطاب، وقال الله تعالى: { فأخرجنا به أزواجا } أصنافا { من نبات شتى } مختلفة الألوان والطعوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may eat the plants and pasture their livestock by letting them graze in the earth's vegetation; this is a lesson for people of reason.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك } الذي ذكرت { لآيات } لعبرة { لأولي النهي } لذوي العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Moses to lead His servants from Egypt at night, strike the sea to make a dry path, and fear neither Pharaoh catching them nor drowning.
rows.anchor: سر بهم ليلا من أرض مصر { فاضرب لهم } بعصاك { طريقا في البحر يبسا } يابسا { لا تخاف دركا } من فرعون خلفك { ولا تخشى } غرقا في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his army pursued them, and the sea overwhelmed and drowned them.
rows.anchor: فلحقهم { فرعون بجنوده فغشيهم من اليم } فعلاهم من البحر { ما غشيهم } ما غرقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying Pharaoh did not guide his people answers Pharaoh's claim that he guides them only to the path of right guidance.
rows.anchor:
رد عليه حيث قال:
وما أهديكم إلا سبيل الرشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved the Israelites from Pharaoh and promised them the Torah at the mountain's right side, where Moses would receive laws and rulings; Moses had promised them he would go there after leaving them.
rows.anchor: لإيتاء الكتاب { جانب الطور الأيمن } وذلك أن الله سبحانه وعد موسى أن يأتي هذا المكان، فيؤتيه كتابا فيه الحلال والحرام والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manna and quail were sent to the Israelites in the wilderness.
rows.anchor: ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى } يعني: في التيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites were told to eat lawful provisions and not transgress by showing ingratitude for the blessing; God's anger then becomes due, and whoever incurs it perishes in the abyss.
rows.anchor: حلالات { ما رزقناكم ولا تطغوا } ولا تكفروا النعمة { فيه فيحل } فيجب { عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل } [يجب]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives whoever repents from shirk, believes in God, does righteous deeds in obedience, and remains guided in that state until death.
rows.anchor: من الشرك { وآمن } وصدق بالله { وعمل صالحا } بطاعة الله { ثم اهتدى } أقام على ذلك حتى مات عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses hastened ahead of the seventy chosen men out of eagerness for God's appointment and ordered them to follow.
rows.anchor: يعني: السبعين الذين اختارهم، وذلك أنه سبقهم شوقا إلى ميعاد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says that his people are following his tracks and that he hurried ahead so God would be more pleased with him.
rows.anchor: قال: هم أولاء على أثري } يجيئون بعدي { وعجلت إليك } بسبقي إياهم { لترضى } لتزداد عني رضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He tested Moses' people after his departure and that al-Samiri led them astray by calling them to worship the calf.
rows.anchor: أي: ألقيناهم في الفتنة واختبرناهم { من بعدك } من بعد خروجك من بينهم { وأضلهم السامري } بدعائهم إلى عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses returned extremely angry and sad; God's good promise was the Torah, and the people broke their promise by making the calf rather than waiting for him, bringing God's anger upon themselves.
rows.anchor: مدة مفارقتي إياكم { أم أردتم أن يحل } أن يجب { عليكم غضب من ربكم فأخلفتم موعدي } باتخاذ العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows best what they say; the fairest in judgment among them will say they remained only a day.
rows.anchor: أعدلهم قولا { إن لبثتم إلا يوما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People asked the Prophet what would happen to the mountains on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: سألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف تكون الجبال يوم القيامة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will scatter the mountains like dispersed dust until they become level with the earth.
rows.anchor: يصيرها كالهباء المنثور حتى تستوي مع الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth will become a level, even place.
rows.anchor: فيذرها قاعا صفصفا } مكانا مستويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There will be no low place or raised elevation on the earth.
rows.anchor: لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا } انخفاضا وراتفاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People follow the caller to the gathering place for Judgment Day and cannot refuse to follow.
rows.anchor: الذي يدعوهم إلى موقف القيامة، ولا يقدرون ألا يتبعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Voices fall silent before the Merciful, so the only sound heard is the footfall of people walking to the gathering.
rows.anchor: سكنت { الأصوات للرحمن فلا تسمع إلا همسا } وطء الأقدام في نقلها إلى المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession benefits only those for whom the Merciful permits intercession: Muslims whose profession that there is no god but God He accepts.
rows.anchor: إلا من أذن له الرحمن } في أن يشفع له، وهم المسلمون الذين رضي الله قولهم؛ لأنهم قالوا: لا إله إلا الله، وهذا معنى قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What lies ahead is the afterlife and what lies behind is worldly life.
rows.anchor: من أمر الآخرة { وما خلفهم } في أمر الدنيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative is that God knows what people have done and what they leave behind.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما قدموا وما خلفوا من خير وشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People do not encompass this knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولا يحيطون به علما } وهم لا يعلمون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faces submit and are humbled before the Living, the Sustainer; ruined is whoever bore the wrong of associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: خضعت وذلت { للحي القيوم وقد خاب من حمل ظلما } خسر من أشرك بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer who does righteous deeds and affirms Muhammad's message need not fear extra sins being counted or good deeds being reduced.
rows.anchor: الطاعات لله { وهو مؤمن } مصدق بما جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { فلا يخاف ظلما ولا هضما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sijill is an angel who folds the books of Adam's children as the sky is folded.
rows.anchor: وهو ملك يطوي كتب بني آدم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes al-sijill as a sheet or scroll, folded over what is written on it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: السجل: الصحيفة، والمعنى: كطي السجل على ما فيه من المكتوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God originated the first creation, He will resurrect people barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised.
rows.anchor: كما خلقناكم ابتداء حفاة عراة غرلا، كذلك نعيدكم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection is a promise God has made and will fulfill.
rows.anchor: أي: وعدناه وعدا { إنا كنا فاعلين } يعني: الإعادة والبعث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Al-Zabur refers to the revealed books that came after the Torah.
rows.anchor: قيل: في الكتب المنزلة بعد التوراة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-dhikr means the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالذكر اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth that God's righteous servants inherit is the earth of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن الأرض } يعني: أرض الجنة { يرثها عبادي الصالحون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, this means the earthly world will pass to believers from Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أرض الدنيا تصير للمؤمنين من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran provides attainment of one's goal for people who worship and obey God.
rows.anchor: لوصولا إلى البغية { لقوم عابدين } مطيعين لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent as mercy to both righteous and wicked: obedience brings swift mercy, while disobedience and denial do not bring worldly punishment as befell earlier rejecting nations.
rows.anchor: للبر والفاجر، فمن أطاعه عجلت له الرحمة، ومن عصاه وكذبه لم يلحقه العذاب في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people turn away from Islam, the Prophet is to warn them on equal terms according to revelation, concealing nothing from one group that he reveals to another.
rows.anchor: عن الإسلام { فقل آذنتكم على سواء } أعلمتكم بما يوحى إلي على سواء لتستووا في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not know whether the promised Judgment Day is near or far.
rows.anchor: ما أعلم { أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون } يعني: القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay of punishment may be a test for the people and a respite for their enjoyment until death.
rows.anchor: لعل تأخير العذاب عنكم { فتنة } اختبار لكم { ومتاع إلى حين } إلى حين الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is commanded to ask for a just judgment between himself and Mecca's people, as earlier messengers asked God to judge between them and their people.
rows.anchor: اقض بيني وبين أهل مكة بالحق، أمر أن يقول كما قالت الرسل قبله من قولهم: { ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to say that the Merciful is the one whose help is sought against their lies and false claims.
rows.anchor: أي: وقل ربنا { الرحمن المستعان على ما تصفون } من كذبكم وباطلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sacrificial animals offer riding, milk, and offspring until their owner designates them as an offering; their slaughter place is the whole sanctuary.
rows.anchor: الركوب والدر والنسل { إلى أجل مسمى } وهو أن يسميها هديا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every previous community was given a rite of animal sacrifice so they would invoke God's name over the livestock He provided.
rows.anchor: جماعة سلفت قبلكم { جعلنا منسكا } ذبحا للقرابين { ليذكروا اسم الله } عند الذبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is one, so people should invoke no name over sacrifices except His, devote worship to Him, and give good tidings to the humble.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تذكروا على ذبائحكم إلا الله وحده { فله أسلموا } أخلصوا العبادة { وبشر المخبتين } المتواضعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-budn means camels and cattle; they are signs of God's religion and bring worldly benefit and otherworldly reward.
rows.anchor: الإبل والبقر { جعلناها لكم من شعائر الله } أعلام دينه { لكم فيها خير } النفع في الدنيا، والأجر في العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At slaughter, people invoke God's name by saying Allahu akbar, there is no god but Allah, and Allahu akbar; the animals stand with their left foreleg tied.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يقول عند نحرها: الله أكبر، لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر { صواف } قائمة معقولة اليد اليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the animals collapse, people may eat their meat and feed those who ask and those who approach without asking.
rows.anchor: سقطت على الأرض { فكلوا منها وأطعموا القانع } الذي يسألك { والمعتر } الذي يتعرض لك ولا يسألك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subdued the animals so people would obey Him in gratitude.
rows.anchor: { كذلك } الذي وصفنا { سخرناها لكم } يعني: البدن { لعلكم تشكرون } لكي تطيعوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists smeared the Kaaba's walls with sacrificial blood, but neither meat nor blood reaches God.
rows.anchor: كان المشركون يلطخون جدار الكعبة بدماء القرابين، فقال الله تعالى: { لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What reaches God is piety, meaning sincere intention for His sake; people magnify God for guiding them to the signs of His religion, and good news is for monotheists.
rows.anchor: { ولكن يناله التقوى منكم } أي: النية والإخلاص وما أريد به وجه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No community dies before its appointed term or outlives it even by a moment.
rows.anchor: لا تموت قبل أجلها { وما يستأخرون } بعد الأجل طرفة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tatra means that successive communities came one after another; God made them stories that later peoples recount.
rows.anchor: أي: متتابعة { وجعلناهم أحاديث } أي: لمن بعدهم يتحدثون بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's people were arrogant, domineering, and unjustly oppressive toward others.
rows.anchor: مستكبرين قاهرين غيرهم بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptians were obedient and submissive to Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: وقومهما لنا عابدون } أي: مطيعون متذللون
